_comment: ngsolve time_dependent_ns#4 (enclosed-flow pressure is determined only up to a constant). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: Stokes on the unit square maxh 0.25, Taylor-Hood VectorH1 order 2 * H1 order 1, no-slip everywhere, singular values of the free-DOF block computed densely. The unconstrained system has exactly ONE singular value at 4.3e-16 against a next one at 6.2e-4, its right singular vector puts 100% of its norm in the pressure block with a relative spread of 3.7e-14, so it is the constant-pressure mode; pinning one pressure DOF removes exactly that one degree of freedom and leaves the smallest singular value at 2.6e-5. CORRECTION: the claim's Signal names PETSc's 'KSPSolve: DIVERGED_BREAKDOWN'. NGSolve does not go through PETSc here and the default umfpack path emits NOTHING -- no exception, no warning, no line on stdout or stderr, checked at the file-descriptor level so C++ output cannot escape -- and returns a finite vector. An agent watching for DIVERGED_BREAKDOWN sees a clean solve on a singular system. The two solutions' velocities agree to 7.5e-18 and their pressures differ by a constant (mean -0.271, variance 1.1e-30), which is the only visible symptom. Mutation: pinning the pressure in the unconstrained branch too removes the nullspace and the fixture fails on exactly_one_zero_mode.
